app.title: calypso: a parameter-conditioned stochastic timeseries emulator (Streamlit demo)
app.summary: A person sets the physical parameters of a system with sliders and picks an observing band. A trained stochastic surrogate model draws synthetic realisations at those parameters, and a physical model turns them into observable magnitudes. The interface plots the individual realisations and a mean ± 1σ band for the whole system and for each of its two components, with the survey's detection limit shaded in. The person can switch the uncertainty model on or off, change how many draws to show or average, and resample to see a fresh set. What they get is a feel for how the shape and spread of the predicted signal change across parameter space.

task.text: Generate synthetic observable time series from a stochastic surrogate model at chosen parameters, to see how their shape, spread and detectability change.

data.text: Synthetic time series sampled from a model trained on simulations: several stochastic realisations per parameter setting, each with a total and two component series, converted to magnitudes in one photometric band.
data.item: one simulated lightcurve realisation at a single parameter setting

stage.text: exploring a trained surrogate model's predictions across parameter space, before using it for forecasts or inference

mechanism.text: Sidebar sliders and checkboxes set the model parameters and display options. Every change reruns a cached pipeline (emulator draws, then disk luminosity, then magnitudes) and redraws two stacked line charts that share a time axis: one for the total, one for the two components. Each chart overlays the faint individual draws, a mean ± std band and a shaded detection-limit region.

field.text: stochastic surrogate emulation of simulated accretion lightcurves, with synthetic survey photometry, in astrophysics

workflow.name: sample a stochastic model at chosen parameters and see the spread of its outputs

steps.here: An expanded 'About calypso' panel explains the PCA basis, the Gaussian over each training binary and the Cholesky interpolation, and notes that epistemic uncertainty can be toggled.

steps.step: set the parameters the model is conditioned on
steps.here: Sliders for eccentricity, mass ratio, log total mass, log separation, redshift and Eddington fraction, bounded to the range the model was trained on.

steps.step: choose what to show and how many samples to draw
steps.here: Choose an LSST band, turn epistemic uncertainty on or off, show or hide the individual realisations (1–64) and the mean ± std band (8–256 samples).

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The emulator samples accretion-rate series, alpha-disk minidisk radii and blackbody emission are integrated over the redshifted band, and the result is converted to AB magnitudes for the total, primary and secondary.

steps.step: compare the realisations and their spread against a threshold
steps.here: Stacked panels overlay the draws, with alpha scaled to how many there are, and the mean ± 1σ band, against a pink band below the single-visit detection limit.

steps.step: draw a fresh set of samples
steps.here: The Resample button increments the random seed so new realisations are drawn at the same parameters.

distinctive: The model is stochastic, so a parameter setting gives a distribution of curves. The interface shows individual draws and a mean ± 1σ envelope together, and draws them from a shared, seeded sample pool.
Epistemic (model) uncertainty can be switched on to see how much it widens the spread beyond the intrinsic variability.
The emulated rates are turned into observable magnitudes by a physical model (thin-disk temperature, blackbody emission, a band shifted by redshift, cosmological distance).
The survey's single-visit magnitude limit is shaded, so the person can see whether the variability would be detectable.
The total signal and its two component series are shown in separate stacked panels that share a time axis in years.
